title: A book of scenarios that keeps the planning cycle's rules

blocks.text: A water utility (a fictional one) keeps its planning scenarios in a **book**: a dictionary from a scenario's name to a record `{"stage", "inputs", "plan", "parent"}`. Its planning cycle has the four stages Initial, Pre-Opt, Post-Opt and Budget Lock, and the book must refuse any step that breaks the cycle. Each function returns `True` when it did the step and `False` when it refused, and a refused step changes nothing.

items: `create(book, name, inputs)`: a new scenario in Initial, with its own copy of `inputs`, no plan and no parent. A name already in the book is refused.
`checked(book, name)`: the data checks passed, so an Initial scenario moves to Pre-Opt.
`optimized(book, name, plan)`: a run finished, so a Pre-Opt scenario moves to Post-Opt and keeps the plan.

`edit(book, name, changes)`: update the inputs with `changes`. A scenario in Budget Lock refuses. An edit to a scenario in Post-Opt makes its plan out of date: it goes back to Pre-Opt and loses its plan. In Initial or Pre-Opt the stage stays as it is.
`lock(book, name)`: a Post-Opt scenario becomes the plan of record. There is only ever one: while any scenario of the book is in Budget Lock, every other lock is refused.
`copy(book, source, name)`: a new scenario in Initial whose inputs start as the source's, with no plan and `parent` set to the source. Editing either one must never change the other.

blocks.text: Any scenario may be copied, whatever its stage; copying a locked plan of record is how a change after lock starts. `create` and `copy` refuse a new name that is already in the book. Every other name the functions receive (the scenario to check, run, edit, lock, or copy from) is one the book has: the tests never pass an unknown one, and the reference simply looks it up, so an unknown name raises `KeyError`.
Before you code, draw the four stages and mark which function moves a scenario along each arrow, and which arrows go back. About thirty lines.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from book import checked, copy, create, edit, lock, optimized

book = {}
print("create 'lean':", create(book, "lean", {"budget": 750}))
print("optimize before checks:", optimized(book, "lean", {"P4": 2030}))
print("checked, optimized:", checked(book, "lean"), optimized(book, "lean", {"P4": 2030}))
print("edit after optimizing:", edit(book, "lean", {"budget": 700}), book["lean"]["stage"], book["lean"]["plan"])
checked(book, "lean")
optimized(book, "lean", {"P4": 2031})
print("lock 'lean':", lock(book, "lean"), book["lean"]["stage"])
print("copy to 'lean-b':", copy(book, "lean", "lean-b"), book["lean-b"])
print("edit locked 'lean':", edit(book, "lean", {"budget": 650}))

cases.says: a scenario goes from Initial to Pre-Opt, Post-Opt and Budget Lock, keeping its plan
a step taken from the wrong stage, or a duplicate name, is refused and changes nothing
a locked scenario refuses edits, and its copy starts over and accepts them
an edit after a run sends the scenario back to Pre-Opt and drops its plan
editing a copy leaves the scenario it was copied from unchanged
a second scenario cannot be locked while one plan of record exists

origin.section: Budget Lock Freezes the Plan of Record, and a Change Means a New Scenario

concepts: Initial, Pre-Opt, Post-Opt and Budget Lock each allow different changes, and steps happen in order
a locked plan of record refuses edits, and a change goes to a copy with its own inputs
an edit after a run sends the scenario back to Pre-Opt and invalidates its plan
